pr_title: kernel: work: Return error if timeout cannot be aborted
pr_body:
This is aligned with the documentation which states that an error shall
be returned if the work has been completed:

  '-EINVAL Work item is being processed or has completed its work.'

Fixes #22803

Signed-off-by: Luiz Augusto von Dentz <luiz.von.dentz@intel.com>
pr_comments: `k_delayed_work_cancel()` and `k_delayed_work_submit_to_queue()` (which is the function called out of the timeout) both operate under the work_q spinlock.  It's not possible for them to see each other in an intermediate state.  The code as-is looks safe to me, unless I'm missing something.

Does this check need to be considered?
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/22810/files#diff-ed0b4d3815d3ce00b451fa30ed3c2051R127-R129

I thought maybe that was where the check failed, because that is reset to NULL when we cancel, but not after it has been submitted to the workqueue and successfully processed as far as I can tell. But I cannot really see that it would lead to any issues.

**All checks are passing now.**

issue_context.title: k_delayed_work_cancel documentation inconsistent with behavior
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/c6d37eba7bf82df12e41b2c4b65cc17d739ea48d/include/kernel.h#L3117 inaccurately documents the behavior of `k_delayed_work_cancel()`.  Specifically, if the work item has already completed the function will return zero, rather than `-EINVAL`.  Assuming the states of a work item:
* never submitted
* delayed
* pending
* processing
* completed
* cancelled

the only time `-EINVAL` would be observed is in never-submitted, cancelled, or if it transitioned from pending to processing during the cancellation attempt.

The intent may have been to implement to the documentation; in that case the `work_q` value must be set to null after processing (which may be risky), and possibly other conditions need to be reviewed.

This had an impact in #22756 where it is not possible to determine whether a pending operation has been completed without maintaining an external flag.
comments:
Thanks.

For my use-case I think a function similar to k_work_pending for k_delayed_work would have been very useful. Between the timeout running out (k_delayed_work_remaining_get) and the timeout handler submitting (or not processed) it's no possible to check if the delayed work has been submitted, but not completed.

review_comments: Yep, it probably make sense to have them both returning -EALREADY so the application can safely resubmit if needs to, as oppose to -EINVAL which indicates that something went wrong and the work is still in progress.

Hmm, I might as well add a comment why we need to handle -EALREADY here since that is likely a resubmit case where the caller is just reusing the same work otherwise we would have to use k_work_init after every work is completed.
